Regarding the physical therapy plan for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow), the prescribed approach is highly effective and aligns with current clinical best practices. Lateral epicondylitis is primarily a tendinopathy involving the extensor carpi radialis brevis tendon, often characterized by degenerative changes rather than acute inflammation. Therefore, the inclusion of eccentric strengthening exercises is critical, as this modality has strong evidence supporting its ability to remodel tendon tissue, improve load tolerance, and reduce pain over time. Manual therapy can be beneficial in the short term to address associated soft tissue restrictions and improve joint mobility, thereby facilitating better exercise mechanics. The use of ice therapy post-workout is also appropriate as a symptomatic management tool to control any acute inflammatory response or soreness resulting from the new loading stimulus, although it does not address the underlying tendon pathology. Overall, this combination of active rehabilitation (eccentric exercise) with supportive modalities (manual therapy and ice) represents a comprehensive and evidence-based strategy for recovery.
